record.title: Motion-gated rhythm classification for a wearable optical pulse sensor

text.abstract: A wearable optical pulse sensor discards a pulse window when accelerometer motion during the window exceeds a motion limit, and classifies an accepted window as irregular when the variability of its beat-to-beat intervals exceeds a threshold. A notice is raised for each irregular window. When the pulse amplitude is low, the sensor may raise the brightness of its light source.
claims: 1. A method comprising: rejecting a pulse window from a wearable optical sensor when accelerometer motion during the window exceeds a motion limit; and classifying an accepted window as irregular when the variability of its beat-to-beat intervals exceeds a threshold.
2. The method of claim 1, comprising raising a notice for each irregular window.

record.title: Motion-gated rhythm classification for a wrist-worn optical pulse sensor

text.abstract: A wrist-worn optical pulse sensor rejects a pulse window when accelerometer motion exceeds 0.1 g and classifies an accepted window as irregular from the variability of its beat-to-beat intervals.
claims: 1. A wrist-worn device comprising an optical pulse sensor and an accelerometer, configured to reject a pulse window when accelerometer motion during the window exceeds 0.1 g, and to classify an accepted window as irregular when the variability of its beat-to-beat intervals exceeds a threshold.

record.title: Confirming an irregular pulse notice with an electrocardiogram

text.abstract: When a watch reports two or more irregular-rhythm episodes within 48 hours, it displays a notice and prompts the user to record an electrocardiogram by touching the crown electrode. The notice is marked confirmed only when the electrocardiogram also shows an irregular rhythm.
claims: 1. A method comprising: when two or more irregular-rhythm episodes are reported within 48 hours, prompting the user of a watch to record an electrocardiogram; and marking a notice confirmed only when the electrocardiogram shows an irregular rhythm.

record.title: Night-time pulse sampling and a personal rhythm baseline

text.abstract: A wearable detects sleep as a period with no movement and a heart rate near its nightly minimum. During sleep it samples a pulse window at fixed intervals and builds a baseline of the wearer's rhythm irregularity over a number of nights.
claims: 1. A method comprising: detecting sleep from the absence of movement and a heart rate near its nightly minimum; sampling a pulse window at fixed intervals during sleep; and building a baseline of the wearer's rhythm irregularity over a plurality of nights.

record.title: Flagging a night that departs from a personal rhythm baseline

text.abstract: Building on a baseline of the wearer's night-time rhythm irregularity, a wearable flags a night whose irregularity exceeds the baseline by more than a set number of standard deviations.
claims: 1. A method comprising: building a baseline of a wearer's night-time rhythm irregularity over a plurality of nights; and flagging a night whose irregularity exceeds the baseline by more than a set number of standard deviations.
